item.title: Milo J & Trueno Double Down on Their Argentine Roots at LAMC: ‘The Best Thing We Could Do Was Make Music With Our Identity’
item.description:
Here's a short and engaging podcast script based on the article:
[INTRO MUSIC FADES OUT]
Host: Welcome to "The Beat", a podcast where we dive into the world of music and explore the latest trends and insights. I'm your host, [Name], and today we're talking about the power of authenticity in Latin music.
Recently, at the Latin Alternative Music Conference, Argentine artists Milo J and Trueno sat down with Billboard's Leila Cobo to discuss their approach to music. And what they had to say was fascinating. According to Milo J, the key to their success is making music that's rooted in their truth, their neighborhoods, and their language.
[CLIP OF MILO J'S QUOTE] Milo J: "The best thing we could do was make music with our identity."
Host: That's right. And Trueno took it a step further, saying that the world listening to their music is a consequence of being true to themselves.
[CLIP OF TRUENO'S QUOTE] Trueno: "The world listening to us is a consequence."
Host: Both artists emphasized the importance of staying authentic and protecting their unique voice. They also talked about the role of soccer culture and neighborhood life in shaping their music and identity.
But it's not all about creativity and inspiration. Milo J and Trueno also shared some valuable advice on the business side of things, from learning about contracts and legal protection to surrounding yourself with trustworthy people.
And in a particularly interesting moment, they expressed caution about the use of artificial intelligence in music. While they see it as a useful tool for demos and references, they believe it can't replace the value of human experience and the process of creating music from scratch.
[OUTRO MUSIC FADES IN]
Host: Thanks for tuning in to this episode of "The Beat". Milo J and Trueno are definitely two artists to watch, with their unique sound and commitment to authenticity. Check out their latest releases, including Milo J's album "La Vida Era Más Corta" and Trueno's LP "TURR4ZO". Until next time, stay true to the beat!
